title: Dashboards + alerts for Dedicated staged rollout gate health (evaluator latency, paused rollouts, per-pool stage)
author: Allison Grant
body:
Summary: Adds first-pass dashboards and alerting for Dedicated staged rollouts gate evaluation health and rollout stuck/paused conditions. This is intended to support dogfood + beta readiness and address oncall feedback that we currently have no quick way to tell whether a rollout is actually unhealthy vs. the evaluator/metrics pipeline being behind. What’s included: 1) Grafana dashboard: “Dedicated Rollouts / Gate Evaluator Health” with panels for evaluator tick latency, evaluation duration, missing-metrics holds, and evaluation success rate (by pool and by tenant, with cardinality controls). 2) Grafana dashboard: “Dedicated Rollouts / Per-pool Stage Status” showing current stage, requested vs effective weights, and gate status rollups (pass/hold/fail) for each stage over time. 3) Alert rules (Prometheus): GateEvaluatorLagHigh (page), GateEvaluatorStalled (page), RolloutPausedTooLong (ticket), MissingMetricsHoldSpike (ticket), and RolloutStageStuckTransition (ticket). 4) Links to runbooks and common triage queries embedded in dashboard annotations + alert annotations (points to Confluence runbook-dedicated-staged-rollout-paused and internal oncall playbook section). Context / motivation: We saw multiple cases in staging/dogfood where rollouts were paused due to missing metrics while the pool was otherwise stable, and one case where evaluator lag delayed a stop-the-line pause. These dashboards/alerts are the observability baseline before enabling staged rollouts for beta tenants (see ENG-5131). Key design notes: - Cardinality: all dashboard queries use pool_id and tenant_id only where required, with an optional “top N pools by traffic” variable to avoid expensive wide scans. We explicitly do NOT slice by model_id, route, or stage_id in alerting. - Alert semantics: evaluator health pages only when we believe the system is blind (lag/stalled). Rollout health is tickets by default; we page only if the observability/control signal is degraded. - Paused rollouts: we alert on paused rollouts exceeding threshold time only when evaluator is healthy; otherwise we’d spam during telemetry outages. - Missing metrics: MissingMetricsHoldSpike is a ticket-level alert intended to catch config regressions (e.g., a newly required metric not being emitted in a region). Screenshots: (internal) Dashboard preview links are in the checklist below. Test plan: - Applied rules in staging stack and validated firing behavior by simulating evaluator downtime (scale to 0) and delaying metrics ingest. - Validated queries against a busy dedicated pool to confirm panel load times remain <2s with default variables. - Confirmed alert annotations render runbook links and include pool_id/tenant_id when present. Rollout plan: Land behind existing observability-pack release process; SRE to enable paging routes after dogfood week completes. Follow-ups (out of scope): - Add per-region breakdown for evaluator lag once we have stable region labeling from ENG-5125. - Add “quality gate” panels when/if quality signals ship for select tenants. - Add a synthetic canary for gate evaluator loop (separate work). Checklist: - [x] Dashboards added and provisioned via jsonnet - [x] Alerts added with runbook links + severity labels - [x] Queries reviewed for cardinality/efficiency - [x] Staging validation complete - [x] SRE sign-off requested (Sean/Rafael) Related: - redwood PRs: gate evaluator service + fail-safe hold behavior (pr_28490, pr_28572), telemetry plumbing (pr_28503, pr_28640) - Linear: ENG-5131 (dashboards + alerts), INT-1133 (missing metrics causes perpetual hold)

Commits: 1) dashboards: add gate-evaluator-health dashboard 2) dashboards: add per-pool-rollout-status dashboard 3) alerts: add evaluator lag/stall paging rules 4) alerts: add paused rollouts + missing-metrics hold spike tickets 5) docs: add dashboard index + runbook links in annotations

Changed areas (high level): - grafana/dashboards/dedicated_rollouts_gate_evaluator_health.jsonnet - grafana/dashboards/dedicated_rollouts_per_pool_stage_status.jsonnet - prometheus/alerts/dedicated_rollouts_gate_evaluator.rules.yaml - prometheus/alerts/dedicated_rollouts_rollout_state.rules.yaml - README.md (dashboard catalog + ownership)

Review conversation (highlights): - Sean Gallagher: “Please ensure RolloutPausedTooLong doesn’t fire when evaluator is unhealthy; otherwise we’ll page/ticket during telemetry incidents.” Author: “Updated expression to gate on evaluator_healthy==1 and added a note in the runbook annotation.” - Logan Wright: “Pool/tenant labels look ok, but avoid stage_id in alert labels. Also, query uses rate over stage transition metric—verify it exists in all regions.” Author: “Removed stage_id from alert labels; switched to rollout_state gauge + transition counter with absent() guard. Confirmed metric present in us-east + eu-west; added ‘absent for 10m’ clause to prevent false fires.” - Thomas Baird: “Panel 6 does join across two series; can we reduce the join cardinality?” Author: “Reworked to pre-aggregate by pool_id before join, and added a topk() around high-volume pools for default view.” - Rafael Mendes: “Runbook link should point to the paused rollout runbook and include ‘metrics freshness’ triage step.” Author: “Updated annotations and added quick links to ‘metrics lag’ dashboard section.”

Merge: Squashed and merged to main.
